dr.upgrading: Some nodes do not support DR plans yet ({{nodes}}). Upgrade them before changing or running plans.

plans.description: Recovery plans bring the VMs of a remote (production) cluster back up on this cluster, group by group.
plans.newDescription: Pick the production cluster, the boot groups and how networks and IPs change on this cluster.
plans.emptyHint: Replicate backups of a remote cluster here, then make a plan, test it, and fail over when disaster strikes.

test.title: Test failover of {{name}}
test.description: Restores the plan's VMs into isolated networks on this cluster and measures the RTO. The source is not touched. Clean up afterwards.
test.notIsolated: These test networks can reach outside (bridge, uplink or router): {{networks}}. Test VMs keep the production IPs and host names.
test.allowRouted: I understand — run the test on these networks anyway

failover.title: Fail over {{name}}
failover.description: The VMs of {{source}} are restored and started on this cluster in group order, with this plan's networks and IPs.

modeHint.planned: The source must be reachable: its VMs are shut down in reverse group order (forced off after 5 minutes — then only crash-consistent), backed up once more and replicated here first. It moves all VMs or none — if any VM cannot be prepared, nothing is recovered here and the stopped VMs are started again on the source.
modeHint.disaster: Use the newest recovery point already on this cluster. The source is not contacted.

failover.disasterWarning: Anything written on the source after its last replicated backup is lost. If the source is still running, both copies will run — shut it down first. When the source comes back, its VMs may start by themselves: isolate it before reconnecting.
failover.after: HA stays off on the recovered VMs. Turn it on after the failover.
failover.preemptsTest: A test of this plan is running: it is cancelled first, and its cleanup starts after the failover.
failover.verifyFailed: Newest copy failed verification (an older one is used): {{vms}}

cleanup.title: Clean up the test of {{name}}
cleanup.description: Stops and deletes the VMs the last test made and removes its isolated networks. VMs made by a failover are not touched.

cancel.title: Cancel the run of {{name}}
cancel.description: The run stops after the current step; running tasks finish.
cancel.afterTest: When the test ends, its cleanup starts by itself.
cancel.afterFailover: VMs the failover already made stay (they are not deleted).
cancel.afterCleanup: Whatever is not deleted yet stays for the next cleanup.
cancel.afterPlanned: Source VMs it stopped are started again (they stay stopped if the source cannot be reached).

delete.description: Deletes the plan and its run history. VMs and networks it made stay.

reprotect.title: Reprotect {{name}}
reprotect.description: Creates backup schedule {{job}} for the recovered VMs that replicates to the remote, to prepare failing back.
reprotect.backupPoolHint: Backup pool here that keeps the recovered VMs' backups
reprotect.keepHint: Old backups beyond these counts are deleted. All zero keeps every backup.

edit.sourceHint: The production cluster the VMs run on now (registered as a remote). The backup copies it sent here are the recovery points.
edit.folderHint: Folder for VMs made by a failover. Empty: the backed up VM's folder.
edit.rpoHint: Alert when the newest copy is older than this. For example 24 warns when more than a day of data could be lost. 0 turns it off.
edit.onTimeout: When a VM fails or times out
edit.noVms: No VMs in this group yet.
edit.networksHint: Source network → network on this cluster. Unlisted networks keep their name.
edit.securityGroupsHint: Source security group → security group on this cluster. Unlisted groups keep their name.
edit.testNetworksHint: Network used by tests. Unlisted source networks get an isolated SDN network during the test. A test network must not reach production: test VMs keep the production IPs.

notIsolated.failover: Failovers use this network too: the test VMs would meet production with the same IPs.
notIsolated.routed: This network has a router: the test may reach other networks.
notIsolated.provider: This is an uplink (provider) network: the test reaches the physical network.
notIsolated.physical: This is a bridge network, not SDN: it may share a physical L2 with production.

edit.sourceBackupPoolHint: Planned migration: pool on the source for the last backup of a VM that has no earlier backup there. Each VM can override it.
edit.ipHelpInstance: A recovered VM gets a new cloud-init instance-id, so cloud-init runs its first-boot modules again: new SSH host keys, and user-data (users, passwords, runcmd) runs again.
edit.ipHelpNoCloudInit: A guest without cloud-init keeps its IP: the rules do not change it.

pick.title: Add VMs to {{group}}
pick.description: VMs of {{source}} and its copies on this cluster.
pick.noSource: Choose the source cluster first. Only copies on this cluster are listed.
pick.remoteFailed: Could not list the source's VMs ({{error}}). Copies on this cluster are still listed.

invalid.name: Use 1–63 lowercase letters, digits and '-'.
invalid.tooManyVms: A plan has at most 500 VMs.
invalid.duplicateVm: A VM is in more than one group.
invalid.mapHalf: Fill in both names or remove the row.
invalid.mapDuplicate: This source is already mapped above.
invalid.pointInTime: Pick a valid date and time.

report.sourceMissing: Remote {{source}} is not registered. No VM has a recovery point.

run.title: {{kind}} · {{plan}}
run.cancelling: Cancel requested — stopping after the current step.
run.stopping: A VM failed or timed out; the remaining VMs are skipped.
run.openCleanup: Open the cleanup that started after the cancel
run.stalled: No progress for {{time}} (no running task and no bounded wait). Check the steps and tasks below.
run.preempted: A failover of this plan cancelled this test. Its cleanup starts after the failover.
run.preemptedTest: This failover cancelled a running test.
run.stalledPlanned: A step keeps retrying an error. If the source went down during a planned migration, cancel and fail over in disaster mode.
run.leftStopped: Source VMs on {{source}} were left stopped (could not start them again): {{vms}}. Check them on the source and start them by hand.
run.allOrNone: A planned failover moves all VMs or none: preparing failed, so nothing was recovered here and the source VMs this run stopped are started again.
run.readiness: Failover readiness problems (seen by this test)
run.readinessHint: A test recovers onto test networks, so even when it succeeds a real failover can fail for these VMs.
run.lost: Recovered from an older recovery point — {{time}} more data lost.
run.copyError: Live restore could not finish copying the disks (the VM did not get all of them): {{error}}

errors.dr_source_missing: The source remote is not registered on this cluster.
errors.dr_run_active: Another run of this plan is still going. Wait for it or cancel it.
errors.dr_cleanup_required: The last test left VMs or networks behind. Use Clean up first — deleting or testing again would lose track of them.
errors.dr_test_network_required: SDN is not set up here: map every source network in the test network map.
errors.dr_name_taken: A VM with that name already exists here.
errors.dr_source_unreachable: The source cluster cannot be reached. A planned migration needs it; use disaster mode if it is down.
errors.dr_nothing_to_clean: Nothing is left from the last test.
errors.dr_no_recovered_vms: No VMs were recovered by a failover of this plan yet.
errors.dr_missing_recovery_points: VMs without a recovery point: {{vms}}. Choose them to skip or wait until copies arrive here.
errors.dr_test_network_not_isolated: Test networks {{networks}} can reach outside (bridge, uplink or router). Map an isolated network in the plan's test network map, or tick “I understand” to go on.
errors.dr_planned_preflight: The planned migration cannot start; nothing was shut down.
errors.dr_vm_in_other_plan: VM {{vm}} is already in plan {{plan}}. A VM can be in one recovery plan only.

runOptions.pointInTime: Recovery point at or before (local time)
runOptions.pointInTimeHint: Empty: the newest recovery point. Pick a time before ransomware or corruption reached the copies.
runOptions.missing_one: {{count}} VM has no recovery point — choose the VMs to skip.
runOptions.missing_other: {{count}} VMs have no recovery point — choose the VMs to skip.
runOptions.skipHint: Chosen VMs are not recovered (the run ends partial). It does not start while any VM here is not chosen.
runOptions.counting: Counting recovery points at that time…

fence.band: Recovered on this cluster but not stopped on {{source}}: {{vms}}. When {{source}} comes back, these VMs start there too and run twice with the same IPs — fence them.
fence.title: Fence the VMs on {{source}}
fence.description: Forces these VMs off on {{source}} and keeps them stopped there (they do not start again when its nodes come back). The copies running here are not touched.
fence.partial_one: {{count}} VM could not be stopped on the source.
fence.partial_other: {{count}} VMs could not be stopped on the source.

errors.dr_nothing_to_fence: No recovered VMs are waiting to be fenced.
errors.dr_source_unreachable: The source cluster cannot be reached. Fence it when it comes back (before reconnecting its networks), or stop the VMs there by hand.
errors.dr_fence_preflight: The token of the source remote is a viewer token. Register the source here with an operator or admin token (Remotes) and try again.

outcome.different_vm: a different VM with that name — not stopped, removed from the list
outcome.different_cluster: the remote points at another cluster — not stopped (check, then clear the fence)

fence.clearDescription: Does nothing on {{source}}; only empties the list of VMs to fence (alert dr_source_returned resolves). Use it only once failback is done or you have checked that the old VMs on the source are stopped or deleted.

readiness.lastTest_one: The last test found {{count}} VM not ready for a real failover.
readiness.lastTest_other: The last test found {{count}} VMs not ready for a real failover.

preflight.token_role: The token of the source remote is not an admin token — register the source here with an admin token (Remotes).
preflight.no_remote_here: The source has no remote for this cluster — add this cluster as a remote on the source.
preflight.vm_missing: {{vm}} is not on the source — remove it from the plan or use disaster mode.
preflight.no_backup_pool: {{vm}} has no backup on the source — set a source backup pool in the plan.
preflight.no_receiving_pool: This cluster has no backup pool to receive the copies — create one (Storage).
preflight.dr_readiness: This cluster has nothing to restore onto (network map target, security group, pool or node) — fix the plan's maps or create it: {{message}}
preflight.dr_name_taken: This cluster has a VM {{vm}} that this plan did not recover — rename or delete that VM.

step.alreadyRecovered: Already recovered by this plan — skipped.
step.preempted: A failover stopped the test — skipped.

help.intro: A plan to start the VMs of a production site on this cluster, in a set order, when that site stops. Rehearse it first with 'Test', which does not touch production.
help.name: The name of this plan, such as prod-to-dr. It cannot be changed later.
help.pool: The pool on this cluster that holds the recovered VMs' disks. Each VM can pick another pool.
help.onTimeout: What to do when a VM does not start or is not ready in time. Usually 'Continue with the rest'.
help.groupName: The name of this group, such as db, app or web.
help.wait: Which state this group's VMs must reach before the next group starts. For VMs that must come first, such as databases, 'reports its IP' is safest.
help.timeout: How long (seconds) to wait for this group's VMs to be ready. After that the 'When a VM fails or times out' choice applies.
help.delay: Extra seconds to wait after this group is ready before starting the next. Usually 0.
help.reprotectRemote: The remote cluster that receives backup copies of the recovered VMs, so you can move back when the production site returns.
